## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column must be fixed before merge because it returns the time of a latest `started` event, so it reports a start time for processes that are still running. Its documented NULL meaning is also wrong for a process that was started and then cleared.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to `models/processes.sql`, computed from the latest event per process, and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` at the repository root that the description does not mention.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — `finished_at` returns the `started` event time — Process 20, whose latest event is `started` at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, gets that start time as `finished_at` while it is still running. `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows only `created`, `started` and `cleared`, so no event records a finish, yet `models/schema.yml:11` says "Timestamp when the process finished." — Consumers reading `finished_at` treat running processes as finished and get a start time where they expect a completion time. — Fix: Either rename the column to `started_at` and update `models/schema.yml:9-11`, or, if `cleared` is the event that marks completion, derive the value from that event instead.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the NULL meaning documented for `finished_at` — Process 30, started at event 3 and cleared at event 4, gets NULL although the description says "NULL means the process has never been started". `models/processes.sql:10` evaluates `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` on the latest event only, so any later event nulls the column. — Consumers who filter on NULL to find never-started processes also get processes that were started and then cleared.
